title: Fill it up
goal: I can find the volume of a cuboid and the volume of water in a tank. I can find the volume of a stone from how much the water rises.

learn.intro: Volume is the space inside a solid. For a cuboid, volume = length × breadth × height. 1 litre is 1000 cm³. A stone that sinks pushes up the water: the rise × the base area is the stone's volume.

example.problem: The floor of a tank is 30 cm × 20 cm. Water fills it to a depth of 9 cm. A stone sinks and the level rises to 12 cm. Find the volume of the stone.
steps: The water rises 12 - 9 = 3 cm. The stone pushes the water up.
The stone's volume equals the extra water, a block 30 × 20 × 3 cm.
example.answer: The volume of the stone is 1800 cm³.

figure.alt: a tank before and after a stone is put in

howto.title: How to
steps: Find the rise: new depth - old depth.
Volume = base length × base width × rise.
Write the unit: cm³. 1000 cm³ = 1 litre.

try.text: A tank floor is 25 cm × 20 cm. Water stands 10 cm deep. A stone of volume 1500 cm³ sinks in it. Find the new depth of the water. {b} cm
try.explanation: The base area is 25 × 20 = 500 cm². The stone raises the water by 1500 ÷ 500 = 3 cm. The new depth is 10 + 3 = 13 cm.

items.text: A box is built from 1 cm cubes. It has 4 cubes along the length, 3 along the width and 2 layers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: 1 layer has {b} cubes.

parts.label: b
parts.text: There are {b} layers.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The box has {b} cubes. Its volume is {b} cm³.

items.explanation: (a) 4 × 3 = 12 cubes in one layer. (b) The box is 2 cubes high, so 2 layers. (c) 12 × 2 = 24 cubes. Each cube is 1 cm³, so the volume is 24 cm³.

figure.alt: cuboid 9 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm

parts.label: a
parts.text: The volume of the cuboid is {b} cm³.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A cube has edges of 7 cm. Its volume is {b} cm³.

items.text: Find the missing length of each cuboid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The base is 8 cm by 5 cm. The volume is 200 cm³. The height is {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The base is a square. The height is 4 cm. The volume is 144 cm³. Each side of the base is {b} cm.

items.explanation: (a) The base area is 8 × 5 = 40 cm². 200 ÷ 40 = 5 cm. (b) The base area is 144 ÷ 4 = 36 cm². 6 × 6 = 36, so each side is 6 cm.

parts.text: A tank is 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. It holds {b} litres when full.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The water has a volume of {b} cm³.

parts.label: b
parts.text: That is {b} litres.

parts.label: c
parts.text: To fill the tank to the top, {b} litres more are needed.

items.text: A tank floor is 50 cm × 20 cm. The water level is 6 cm. Then 4 litres are poured in.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The water rises {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The water is now {b} cm deep.

items.explanation: The base area is 50 × 20 = 1000 cm². 4 litres = 4000 cm³. The rise is 4000 ÷ 1000 = 4 cm. The new depth is 6 + 4 = 10 cm.

items.text: The floor of a tank is 24 cm × 15 cm and the water is 8 cm deep. A stone sinks and the water level reaches 11 cm. Find the stone's volume. {b} cm³
items.explanation: The rise is 11 - 8 = 3 cm. The volume of the stone is 24 × 15 × 3 = 360 × 3 = 1080 cm³.

items.text: A tank has a base 60 cm by 30 cm. The water is 20 cm deep. Then 9 litres of water are taken out.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The water level falls {b} cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The water is now {b} cm deep.

items.explanation: The base area is 60 × 30 = 1800 cm². 9 litres = 9000 cm³. The fall is 9000 ÷ 1800 = 5 cm. The new depth is 20 - 5 = 15 cm.

items.text: Cuboids are made with 30 cubes, using all the cubes each time. The edges are whole numbers of cm. A cuboid that is turned round is not new.

parts.label: a
parts.text: There are {b} different cuboids.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The cuboid with the smallest total of the 3 edges has a total of {b} cm.

items.explanation: List the sets of 3 edges with product 30: 1, 1, 30; 1, 2, 15; 1, 3, 10; 1, 5, 6; 2, 3, 5. That is 5 cuboids. Their totals are 32, 18, 14, 12 and 10. The smallest is 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 cm.

items.text: A big cube is made from 27 small cubes (3 by 3 by 3). All its outside is painted. Then it is taken apart.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Cubes with 3 painted faces: {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Cubes with 2 painted faces: {b}

parts.label: c
parts.text: Cubes with 1 painted face: {b}

parts.label: d
parts.text: Cubes with no paint: {b}

items.explanation: (a) The 8 corner cubes have 3 painted faces. (b) Each of the 12 edges has 1 middle cube with 2 painted faces. (c) Each of the 6 faces has 1 middle cube with 1 painted face. (d) 1 cube is in the middle with no paint.

items.text: Cubes with edges of 6 cm are packed in neat layers in a carton 32 cm long, 20 cm wide and 14 cm high. The cubes cannot be cut. How many cubes fit in the carton? {b}
items.explanation: Along the length: 32 ÷ 6 = 5 and 2 cm is left over, so 5 cubes. Along the width: 20 ÷ 6 = 3, so 3 cubes. In height: 14 ÷ 6 = 2, so 2 layers. 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubes. (Not 8960 ÷ 216 = 41, because the cubes cannot be cut.)

items.text: A cube-shaped container with edges of 30 cm is full of water. All the water goes into an empty tank with a 60 cm × 45 cm floor. Find the depth of the water in the tank. {b} cm
items.explanation: The water has a volume of 30 × 30 × 30 = 27 000 cm³. The base of the tank is 60 × 45 = 2700 cm². The depth is 27 000 ÷ 2700 = 10 cm.

items.text: A tank is 2/5 full of water. Then 18 litres more go in and the tank is 7/10 full. Find the capacity of the full tank. {b} litres
items.explanation: 7/10 - 2/5 = 7/10 - 4/10 = 3/10 of the tank is 18 litres. So 1/10 is 6 litres and the full tank is 10 × 6 = 60 litres.

items.text: Circle True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.text: 1 litre of water has a volume of 1000 cm³.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: b
parts.text: A cuboid 2 cm × 3 cm × 4 cm has the same volume as a cube with edges of 3 cm.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: c
parts.text: If all 3 edges of a cuboid are doubled, its volume is doubled.   {circ:True|False}

items.explanation: (a) True. (b) The cuboid is 24 cm³. The cube is 27 cm³, so it is false. (c) False: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, so the volume is 8 times as much.

items.text: A big cube is made of small cubes. Its outside is painted. Then it is taken apart. 54 small cubes have exactly 1 painted face. How many small cubes make the big cube? {b}
items.hint: Each face has the same number of 1-face cubes. How many?
items.explanation: The cube has 6 faces. 54 ÷ 6 = 9 one-face cubes on each face. That is a 3 by 3 square in the middle of the face. So each face is 3 + 2 = 5 cubes across. The big cube is 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 small cubes.

items.text: Tank A has a floor 40 cm × 30 cm. Its water is 18 cm deep. Tank B has a floor 30 cm × 20 cm and starts empty. Water is poured from A into B until the 2 tanks have equal depths. Find that depth. {b} cm
items.hint: Add the 2 base areas. The same volume of water spreads over both.
items.explanation: The water in A is 40 × 30 × 18 = 21 600 cm³. After pouring, this water is in both tanks at the same depth. The 2 bases are 1200 cm² and 600 cm², which is 1800 cm² together. The depth is 21 600 ÷ 1800 = 12 cm.

items.text: A tank floor is 40 cm × 20 cm and the water is 9 cm deep. A block 10 cm × 20 cm × 15 cm stands upright on the floor. Find the new water depth. {b} cm

figure.alt: tank with a block standing in it

items.hint: Water cannot go where the block is. Find the free floor area.
items.explanation: The water volume is 40 × 20 × 9 = 7200 cm³. The block covers 10 × 20 = 200 cm² of the floor. The floor left for water is 800 - 200 = 600 cm². The depth is 7200 ÷ 600 = 12 cm. The block is 15 cm tall, so it stands above the water, and the answer is right.

items.text: A solid cube has edges of 6 cm. A tunnel 2 cm by 2 cm goes straight through the middle from the front to the back. 2 more tunnels of the same size go through the middle from left to right and from top to bottom. What is the volume of the solid that is left? {b} cm³
items.hint: Count the tunnel cubes. The middle cubes are in all 3 tunnels.
items.explanation: The cube is 6 × 6 × 6 = 216 small cubes. 1 tunnel has 2 × 2 × 6 = 24 cubes. 3 tunnels have 72 cubes, but the 8 cubes in the middle (2 × 2 × 2) were counted 3 times. The tunnels take away 72 - 2 × 8 = 56 cubes. The solid has 216 - 56 = 160 cm³.

items.text: A tank measures 60 cm × 50 cm × 40 cm and is empty. A tap pours in 9 litres each minute. A leak loses 1 litre each minute. After how many minutes is the tank full? {b}
items.hint: Find the capacity. Then the net litres gained each minute.
items.explanation: The tank holds 60 × 50 × 40 = 120 000 cm³ = 120 litres. Each minute the tank gains 9 - 1 = 8 litres. 120 ÷ 8 = 15 minutes.

items.text: The areas of 3 faces of a cuboid that meet at one corner are 24 cm², 36 cm² and 54 cm². Find the volume of the cuboid. {b} cm³
items.hint: Guess 3 edges whose products in pairs are 24, 36 and 54.
items.explanation: Try edges 4, 6 and 9: 4 × 6 = 24, 4 × 9 = 36 and 6 × 9 = 54. They fit. The volume is 4 × 6 × 9 = 216 cm³.

items.text: A tank floor is 50 cm × 30 cm and the tank holds 18 litres. Find the water depth. {b} cm
items.explanation: 18 litres = 18 000 cm³. The base is 50 × 30 = 1500 cm². The depth is 18 000 ÷ 1500 = 12 cm.

items.text: A cube is made of 64 small cubes (4 by 4 by 4). Its outside is painted. Count the small cubes with exactly 2 painted faces. {b}
items.explanation: The cube has 12 edges. On each edge the 2 middle cubes have 2 painted faces (the 2 end cubes are corners). 12 × 2 = 24.

items.text: A tank floor is 20 cm × 15 cm and the water is 10 cm deep. A stone sinks and the water rises to 14 cm. Find the volume of the stone. {b} cm³
items.explanation: The rise is 14 - 10 = 4 cm. The volume is 20 × 15 × 4 = 300 × 4 = 1200 cm³.
